analysis.investment_thesis: Atlanta Electricals is a genuinely high-quality transformer manufacturer with ~50% ROCE — exactly the kind of business the Magic Formula loves. But the Magic Formula requires both quality AND cheapness, and at a P/E of 73x the earnings yield is only ~1.8% (EBIT INR 194 Cr / EV ~INR 10,772 Cr), far below the 12–15% threshold needed to rank well.
key_strengths: Exceptional capital efficiency: ROCE of 50.1% and ROE of 41% — well above the 25%+ Magic Formula benchmark
Strong revenue growth (33.6% CAGR 4Y) with operating leverage: EBIT CAGR 56.9% outpacing revenue
Low debt historically (D/E 0.46 on 2025 equity of INR 782 Cr) with growing operating cash flow (INR 84 Cr in 2025)
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~1.8% (EBIT/EV) is one-tenth the 15% threshold — wildly overvalued by Magic Formula standards at P/E 73x

Balance sheet nearly tripled in one year (assets INR 559 Cr → INR 1,618 Cr in 2025): capex surged to INR 113 Cr, FCF turned negative (−INR 30 Cr), and borrowings jumped from INR 49 Cr to INR 362 Cr — unclear if returns justify this capital deployment
Profit volatility: Net profit fell from INR 87 Cr (2023) to INR 64 Cr (2024) before recovering — single-year spikes inflate ROIC; need 3+ years of sustained returns post-expansion
red_flags: Note: Provided EV/EBITDA of 9.8x is inconsistent with disclosed data; correct calculation (INR 10,772 Cr EV / INR 198 Cr EBITDA) yields ~54x — a significant data discrepancy
Promoter holding at 87.28% leaves very thin public float, amplifying price volatility and exit risk
Sudden tripling of total assets in FY2025 (likely QIP + aggressive capex) without clear visibility on returns from new capacity
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Using the Magic Formula, Atlanta Electricals scores on only one of two required pillars. The business quality is legitimately excellent: ROCE of 50%, ROE of 41%, and operating margin of 17.45% reflect durable competitive advantages in niche transformer segments (furnace, solar, special duty). Revenue has compounded at 33.6% and EBIT at 56.9% over four years. This is the kind of business Greenblatt wants to own — the problem is exclusively price.

The earnings yield (EBIT/EV) works out to ~1.8% using the available data (EBIT INR 194 Cr, EV ~INR 10,772 Cr). Magic Formula demands 12–15%+ to rank in the top decile; 1.8% is a near-total disqualification. At P/E 73x, the market has already priced in years of exceptional execution. Additionally, FY2025 saw a capital-raise-driven balance sheet explosion (+INR 1 trillion in assets), INR 113 Cr in capex, and negative FCF (−INR 30 Cr) — meaning the high historical ROIC may compress as the new, heavier asset base seasons. The Magic Formula is not for buying great businesses at any price; it is for buying great businesses at great prices. Atlanta Electricals is currently neither cheap nor generating free cash flow.
